intro: Most Buddhists in the world today read texts that are not in the Pali Canon. In East Asia, people chant the Heart Sutra, honor the Lotus Sutra and call the name of Amitabha Buddha. In Tibet, monks study huge collections of translated texts and sing the songs of great yogis. In this unit, you will explore Mahayana sutras, Zen writings and Tibetan texts.

You will read the parable of the burning house, meet the bodhisattva of compassion, and learn what Mahayana teachers mean by emptiness. Then you will look at Zen koans and the Platform Sutra, Dogen's writings, Milarepa's life, the so-called Tibetan Book of the Dead and Shantideva's poem.

By the end, you will be able to explain key ideas like skillful means, emptiness and the bodhisattva path, tell how different schools choose their central texts, and show how a text's meaning can change when it reaches new readers.
bigQuestion: How do Mahayana, Zen and Tibetan Buddhists use their texts, and how have outsiders read them?

timeline.t: Scholars date the first Mahayana sutras to around this time
Nagarjuna develops Madhyamaka thought on emptiness
Kumarajiva translates the Lotus Sutra into Chinese
Xuanzang's Chinese Heart Sutra, as tradition dates it
Huineng's teaching (Platform Sutra); Shantideva writes at Nalanda
Milarepa sings and teaches in Tibet (dates vary)
Dogen writes 'Genjokoan', later part of the Shobogenzo
Tibetan canon organized into Kangyur and Tengyur; Bardo Thodol found
Evans-Wentz publishes The Tibetan Book of the Dead
Zen Flesh, Zen Bones brings Zen stories to English readers

test.q: Which sutra contains the parable of the burning house?
What does the Heart Sutra teach?
choices: Form is emptiness, emptiness is form
Monks must stay put in the rains
test.why: The Heart Sutra is the classic short text on emptiness.

test.q: Who translated the Lotus Sutra into Chinese in 406?
test.why: Kumarajiva's version is most widely read.

choices: Avalokiteshvara, bodhisattva of compassion, in China
test.why: Guanyin is the Chinese name for Avalokiteshvara.

test.q: What do Pure Land Buddhists chant?
choices: Case one of the Gateless Gate

test.q: Which Japanese teacher centered practice on the Lotus Sutra's title?

choices: A puzzling story or question used in Zen training
test.why: Koans are studied in Zen practice.

test.q: Who asked 'What is the sound of one hand?'
test.why: The question comes from Hakuin, not the Gateless Gate.

test.q: Which text tells the story of Huineng?
test.why: The Platform Sutra centers on Huineng.
Marpa tested him with years of labor.

test.q: Why did the title 'The Tibetan Book of the Dead' matter?
choices: It shaped how Western readers saw the text
It changed the text into Pali
test.why: Evans-Wentz's title echoed the Egyptian Book of the Dead.

test.q: What does the popular word 'zen' often leave out?
choices: The tradition's temples, training and texts
test.why: Popular 'zen' keeps only calm, not the Buddhist tradition.

write.prompt: Choose two texts from this unit, such as the Lotus Sutra's burning house (ch. 3) and the Heart Sutra, or the Gateless Gate (case 1) and the Bardo Thodol. Cite each passage with its section and translation. Explain what each text says and how its readers, inside and outside the tradition, have read it.
tips: Name each text, its section, and the translation you used.
Say these passages are paraphrased in your own words.
Attribute beliefs: 'Pure Land Buddhists believe...', 'Zen teachers say...'.
Use unit words like emptiness, skillful means and reception.
